sentences.text: The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — was a small, slender, bipedal animal measuring between 3.5 and 5 meters in length.
Researchers identify this known specimen as a juvenile because its vertebrae and ribs show a lack of fusion.
Unlike other non-hadrosauriforms, Cumnoria has scapula margins that only moderately diverge and lacks a defined cingulum on its dentary teeth.
Cumnoria is known from holotype OXFUM J.3303, a partial skull and postcranium found in the Chawley Brick Pits at Cumnor Hurst.
Harry Govier Seeley established the genus Cumnoria in 1888, naming it after the village of Cumnor where the fossils were found.
David Norman concluded in 1998 that Seeley's original distinction of Cumnoria as a separate genus was valid.
Cumnoria belongs to the class Ornithischia.
The Paleobi Database lists the parent group of Cumnoria as Styracosterna.
If classified as a basal styracostern, Cumnoria would be the oldest known member of that group.
Cumnoria lived during the Late Jurassic period in what is now Oxfordshire, United Kingdom.
Cumnoria lived between 152.21 and 149.2 million years ago during the Kimmeridgian age.
It is debated whether Cumnoria is distinct from Camptosaurus, with some studies synonymizing them while others maintain their separation.
